finding.text: The core/Task readme doesn't mention the new `Task.steps.js` or `Task.steps.test.mjs`, and doesn't say that `TaskView` now accepts `subject`. Item's and List's readmes both name their steps files (Item readme line 90, List readme line 48), so Task's should too (docs gap, Law 9). See `worktree/test-view:public/framework/core/Task/readme.md`, "render() and TaskView".

`ux/Content/Object/doc/default-view.md` "how it stays live" is now out of date. It doesn't describe the two behaviours this diff adds to `DefaultView.update`: a list created after the view was drawn now gets its own row, and a new row lands before the lists. A fresh agent would have to read the diff to learn this (docs gap). See `DefaultView.js` lines 278 and 292 in the diff.

Step text often wraps to 2–3 lines per step, so the "one line of text per step, at most" ask (requirements 5) is only partly met. The `// the X button` comments push the code past one line at 1920. See `shots/view-Task-1920.png`, steps column: "Add two subtasks", "Finish one" and "Finish the last" each take 2 code lines.

The tally breaks a file path in the middle of the name, "Item.steps.te / st.mjs" (wrapping). See `shots/…-Test-view/1920.png`, steps column, the tally line. Put the path in a `code` element on its own line, or shorten it.

The click path presses buttons that the test view makes itself ("Start", "Done: The CSS"). It doesn't press TaskView's real row buttons. Requirement 3 is met as written ("a click calls a verb"), but the comment in `Task.steps.js` calls them "the buttons a task row has", which overstates it.
In the Lines column, steps that wrote nothing still get a full card (Create, Save, Replay: "0 lines"), each about 70px of empty space (spacing). See `shots/…-Test-view/1920.png`, right column.

`Task.clock` is pinned in step 1 and only cleared in the Replay step. If an earlier step throws, the global clock stays pinned for the rest of the page (and the node process). Clearing it in a `finally` inside `Steps.all`, or giving the test an "after" hook, would make it safe.
Both pages log one 404 for a missing resource (`layout.json` errors at both widths). It shows on /framework/core/Test/ as well, so it probably comes from before this diff, but nobody has named it.
